automations.title: Independent #742 Research
automations.prompt:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE — INDEPENDENT ERDOS #742 / MURTY–SIMON PROOF PROGRAMME. Put essentially all forward mathematical effort into a genuinely independent proof that every diameter-2-critical graph G on n vertices satisfies e(G)<=floor(n^2/4), preferably with equality only for K_{floor(n/2),ceil(n/2)}. Do not reconstruct or cosmetically rearrange the external Erdos742/Erdos742 e+disj+X proof; use it only as a benchmark/hostile comparison. Prioritize the project’s complement/residual/Hall/profile/realizability route and the live strip n/2<Delta<7n/12, incorporating any later internally checked threshold improvement only at its audited trust level. Treat balanced complete bipartite graphs as mandatory equality controls. A 24-focused-session go/no-go gate remains binding.

START-OF-RUN. Work in paullenz/MurtySimon742. Before mathematics read CURRENT_STATE.md, README.md, the latest daily audit, project/research/session_logs/SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md, and the current independent-#742 proof/reviewer package. Inherit the latest audit’s verified findings, invalidations, caveats, mandatory constraints and prioritized next steps. Do not revive superseded mathematics without an explicit repair path. Distinguish internal candidate mathematics, exact computation, independent re-derivation, external review and established theorem status.

HARD SLOT IDENTITY — ONE SCHEDULED TRIGGER = ONE SESSION. The unique session identity is the scheduled trigger timestamp in Europe/London, never the invocation, retry, compaction, context re-entry or preservation continuation. At invocation start determine the scheduled trigger it belongs to and use that exact timestamp as session_id. All re-entries/retries belonging to that trigger append to the same canonical telemetry record. NEVER create a second independent session for the same trigger. Preserve historical fragment files but reconcile them into the canonical record and mark them superseded for utilisation accounting.

CANONICAL TELEMETRY. Create/update exactly one canonical file per trigger at project/research/session_logs/YYYY-MM-DD/<scheduled-trigger>-canonical.json, following SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md. Create it BEFORE repository reading or mathematics. It must contain a segments array. Every invocation/re-entry appends a segment with segment_id, actual_start, actual_stop if evidenced, role (forward_research/preservation/reconciliation/late_no_research), and notes. Never overwrite or discard prior segments. Obtain an authoritative Europe/London timestamp before work; record scheduled trigger, earliest actual start, next trigger, research_cutoff, hard_close_deadline and lateness. Never infer actual time from cron.

ANTI-OVERLAP TIMING RULE. The normal next trigger is one hour after the scheduled trigger. Define RESEARCH_CUTOFF = next scheduled trigger minus 7 minutes. Define HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE = next scheduled trigger minus 1 minute. Forward research must stop by RESEARCH_CUTOFF. Preservation, CURRENT_STATE update, telemetry finalization and user-report preparation must be completed by HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE. Do not continue cleanup, reconciliation or optional checking past the hard-close deadline. If something remains unfinished, record it explicitly and leave it to the next audit/reconciliation rather than consuming the next research trigger. The next scheduled trigger is never to be silently skipped because the previous session is still cleaning up.

50-MINUTE TARGET. Target at least 50 VERIFIED minutes of forward research whenever at least 50 minutes are genuinely available from earliest actual start to RESEARCH_CUTOFF. For a normally starting hourly session this target applies. If less than 50 verified minutes are achieved despite >=50 minutes being available, mark the session SHORT/NONCOMPLIANT unless all reasonable mathematical/audit/repair/regression/hostile-example/checker avenues were genuinely blocked by unavailable information/capability. Completion of a theorem, clean checkpoint, context compaction, GitHub write, tool failure or report readiness is not an exception. If the first invocation is late enough that fewer than 50 minutes remain to the research cutoff, target status is N/A but the lateness remains visible. Re-entry never resets the clock or target.

FORWARD-RESEARCH INTERVALS. Every claimed period of forward research must be a closed evidenced [start,stop] interval in the canonical record. On context handoff/compaction, close the current interval if the boundary is actually known. On re-entry, append a new interval to the same record. Missing boundaries are UNVERIFIED and are never inferred from commits, unit count, prose length, report time or schedule. Timestamp substantive units as they complete. The verified forward span is the union of closed non-overlapping intervals only.

SESSION EXECUTION. Do not stop because a single lemma, theorem, checker, computation, repair or subcase has completed. After every substantive unit immediately pursue the highest-value coherent follow-on that fits before RESEARCH_CUTOFF. Tool/infrastructure failure triggers a pivot rather than termination. Prefer depth on the independent #742 strip, graph-to-profile bridge, actual graph realizability and equality stability over unrelated exploration. Preserve failed approaches and hostile examples. Do not treat abstract scalar/profile feasibility as graph realizability.

EARLY-STOP CHECK. Before beginning preservation obtain a fresh authoritative timestamp. If more than 5 minutes remain before RESEARCH_CUTOFF and any sensible mathematical/audit step exists, continue research. Record the check and result. Begin preservation early enough to finish by HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE.

FINALIZATION. Before reporting, finalize the canonical record with: session_id/scheduled_trigger; all segments; earliest actual start; next trigger; research cutoff; hard-close deadline; all closed forward intervals; verified forward span; forward stop; preservation start/complete; wall-clock span; substantive-unit count and timestamped ledger; early-stop check; stop reason; failures/pivots; commit SHAs; unfinished line; target applicability/result; and compliance status. Any mandatory missing/PENDING/inconsistent field makes utilisation UNVERIFIED/NONCOMPLIANT. Never fabricate historical times.

NO LOST HOURS. If old-session preservation or reconciliation somehow reaches the next trigger, it remains attached to the OLD session. The new scheduled trigger still has a distinct session identity and must start a new canonical record. If runtime/infrastructure prevents it from starting, record that trigger as MISSED or LATE with exact evidence; never merge it into the prior hour. Do not use high commit counts or productive surrounding hours to excuse a missed trigger.

HANDOFF. Update CURRENT_STATE.md with a compact mirror of the canonical session: scheduled trigger, earliest actual start, verified forward intervals and total, research cutoff, preservation complete, substantive units, stop reason, target result, compliance status, and canonical telemetry path. Keep README.md current when durable public-facing mathematical status changes. Preserve useful proofs, failed routes, scripts, exact outputs and dependencies. User-facing reports should be concise and end with the exact canonical session-utilisation summary. Finish and return before HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE.

automations.title: Midnight #742 Red-Team Audit
automations.prompt:
Perform the dedicated daily adversarial audit for the independent Erdős #742 / Murty–Simon proof programme in paullenz/MurtySimon742. This audit replaces the normal forward-research hour closest to midnight and must not become a forward-theorem session except for bounded tests needed to validate or falsify claims.

PRIMARY AUDIT OBJECTIVE. Critically assess the previous 24 hours of work toward a genuinely independent proof that every diameter-2-critical graph G on n vertices satisfies e(G)<=floor(n^2/4), with the stronger equality characterization kept in scope. The preferred route is structurally independent of the external Erdos742/Erdos742 e+disj+X proof and is currently centred on closing the maximum-degree strip n/2 < Delta < 7n/12 using the project’s complement / residual / Hall / profile / realizability machinery. The preserved 7/12 theorem is still candidate/internal-review mathematics, not an externally established theorem, so audit its load-bearing graph-to-profile and scalar steps as part of assessing any attempted strengthening.

AUDIT TASKS. Start from CURRENT_STATE.md, README.md, the latest prior audit, recent commits/diffs, all new proof notes, scripts/checkers, exact outputs, and session telemetry. Identify every mathematically material claim promoted or relied on in the last 24 hours. Test assumptions, quantifiers, edge cases, dependency direction, arithmetic, exact computations, graph realizability, equality cases, and consistency with known D2C controls. Search actively for hidden use of the external proof’s core argument that would undermine claimed independence. Distinguish scalar/profile feasibility from actual graph realizability. Pay special attention to any claimed threshold improvement below 7/12, any new rigidity theorem near Delta=n/2, and any treatment of the balanced complete-bipartite equality geometry.

24-SESSION GO/NO-GO GATE. Track the focused-session count since the #742 pivot. The first 24 focused sessions must yield at least one of: a strictly improved maximum-degree threshold; a new rigorously stated rigidity/realizability theorem materially reducing the strip; or a finite-dimensional obstruction with a credible closure path. At the first audit after 24 focused sessions, make an explicit continue/pivot recommendation based on evidence, not sunk cost. Do not silently revert to the previous eventual-D2C objective.

STRICT SESSION-UTILISATION AUDIT. The scheduled trigger timestamp is the unique accounting identity of each hourly research session. Inspect project/research/session_logs/SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md and every telemetry file from the preceding 24 hours. For EACH scheduled trigger, require one canonical telemetry record keyed by that trigger. Reconcile every split/re-entered/compacted/retry/preservation-only fragment into that one canonical record while preserving the fragments as evidence. A fragment is never a second session. If the canonical record is absent, create an audit reconciliation record without fabricating timestamps and mark missing fields UNVERIFIED/NONCOMPLIANT. Do not infer missing duration from commits, unit count, prose, output volume, or nominal schedule.

CANONICAL RECONCILIATION. For each scheduled trigger report: session_id/scheduled trigger; all invocation/re-entry segments; earliest actual start; next trigger; preservation cutoff; each evidenced forward-research interval; total verified forward-research span as the union of closed non-overlapping intervals; forward-research stop; preservation start/complete; wall-clock span; substantive-unit count; early-stop check/result; stop reason; infrastructure failures; lateness; >=50-minute target applicability/result; and compliance status. If a context re-entry lacks a trustworthy boundary, preserve the segment but mark its duration UNVERIFIED. Late preservation belonging to the previous trigger must remain attached to the previous session and must not erase or redefine the next scheduled hour.

NO LOST-HOUR CHECK. Enumerate every scheduled research trigger in the 24-hour audit window whether or not a file exists. Classify each as COMPLIANT, SHORT/NONCOMPLIANT, LATE-START/N/A-TARGET, MISSED/NO-FORWARD-RESEARCH, or UNVERIFIED/MISSING-TELEMETRY, using only evidence. Specifically flag any trigger whose new research session appears to have been displaced by preservation/reconciliation from the prior hour. Do not excuse a missed trigger merely because the surrounding hours contain many commits or substantive units.

AGGREGATE UTILISATION. Calculate aggregate utilisation only from verified closed forward intervals. Report: scheduled session count; canonical records present; fully verified sessions; compliant >=50-minute sessions; short/noncompliant sessions; late-start sessions; missed/zero-forward sessions; unverified/missing sessions; total verified available research-window minutes; total verified forward-research minutes; and verified utilisation percentage over only the windows whose availability and forward intervals are both evidenced. Also report a separate lower-bound total of forward minutes when partial verified intervals exist, clearly labelled as a lower bound rather than full-day utilisation.

REPOSITORY HYGIENE. Ensure CURRENT_STATE.md and README.md accurately state that the active priority is the independent #742 route, while preserving prior eventual-D2C work as historical/reusable research. Correct stale or contradictory status text, links, filenames, theorem labels, confidence claims, or telemetry summaries. Preserve failed approaches, invalidated lemmas, hostile examples, superseded routes, and historical telemetry fragments rather than deleting them. Ensure the canonical telemetry schema is being followed prospectively.

MANDATORY HANDOFF. Before ending, encode the audit outcome into CURRENT_STATE.md so the next forward session automatically inherits: verified findings; weakened/invalidated claims; unresolved risks; confidence changes; focused-session count; mandatory constraints; canonical session-utilisation summary; any missed-hour/process findings; and the prioritized next-hours programme with explicit stop/pivot criteria. Update README.md where durable public-facing status changed. Preserve a dated audit note and PDF summary for a mathematically sophisticated external reader, separating established facts, internal candidate results, exact computation, and conjectural interpretation.

USER OUTPUTS. Produce (1) a concise prioritized next-hours proposal based on the audit, and (2) a polished dated PDF covering what was actually achieved, evidentiary status, threshold/rigidity progress, failures, red-team findings, repo changes, remaining holes, confidence changes, the canonical per-trigger utilisation table and aggregates, and the next 24-hour programme. Include exact commit hashes, filenames, theorem/lemma names and checker identifiers where relevant. Avoid promotional language and do not preserve confidence merely because a route is strategically attractive.
